mission:
Fix a bug: `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js returns true for intervals that only touch at one end when either interval is marked half-open.
Support an optional `open: true` property on an interval, meaning its end point is excluded: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` must be false, while the same call without `open` stays true.
Keep the existing behaviour for intervals without `open`, add regression tests next to the existing ones, and keep `npm test` passing.

plan.summary: `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js (line 3) compares both bounds with `<=` and ignores any `open` property, so intervals touching at an excluded end point are reported as overlapping. The fix is to make each comparison strict when the interval whose `end` is involved has `open: true` (`b.start < a.end` when `a.open`, `a.start < b.end` when `b.open`), leaving the closed-interval path unchanged. Regression tests go in the existing test/overlaps.test.js. The change is two files and one coherent edit, so it is planned as a single worker task.
assumptions: `open: true` excludes only the interval's `end` point; `start` is always included (half-open [start, end)).
The flag applies symmetrically regardless of argument order: an `open` interval in either position excludes its own end, so `overlaps({start:3,end:5}, {start:1,end:3,open:true})` is also false.
An `open` flag on the interval whose end is not the touching point has no effect: `overlaps({start:1,end:3}, {start:3,end:5,open:true})` stays true because 3 is still in both.
Only a truthy `open` changes behaviour; a missing, `false` or `undefined` `open` means closed, as today.
No input validation or special handling of degenerate intervals (e.g. start === end with `open: true`) is required; none exists today and the request does not ask for it.
No README change is needed; README.md only describes the package and the test command.
acceptanceCriteria: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` still returns true.
The two existing tests in test/overlaps.test.js are still present, unmodified and passing.
New regression tests for the `open` behaviour exist in test/overlaps.test.js.
`npm test` exits with code 0 and reports no failing tests.

risks.description: The strict comparison is applied to the wrong side (e.g. made strict whenever either interval is open), which would wrongly report `overlaps({start:1,end:3}, {start:3,end:5,open:true})` as false.
risks.mitigation: The task spells out which comparison depends on which interval's flag and requires a test for an open flag on the non-touching end.

risks.description: The fix only handles the open interval as the first argument, leaving the swapped-argument case broken.
risks.mitigation: A swapped-argument regression test is a required acceptance criterion.

risks.description: Existing closed-interval behaviour regresses, or the existing tests get edited to fit the new code.
risks.mitigation: The two original tests must remain unchanged and passing; the verifier checks the diff of test/overlaps.test.js and runs `npm test`.

risks.description: Semantics of a degenerate half-open interval (start === end with `open: true`, which is empty) are not defined by the request.
risks.mitigation: Left out of scope and recorded as an assumption; no test asserts a result for this case, so it can be decided later without breaking the suite.
